key_insight: LLM-driven, verifiable compilation redesigns Shor’s arithmetic pipeline to bring expected RSA-2048 factoring costs below one billion Toffoli gates.
engineering_relevance: The resulting qubit–Toffoli trade-offs could substantially reduce logical resource requirements for fault-tolerant quantum factoring.
method: Use LLM-driven search to optimize the approximate residue number system pipeline across arithmetic stages.
Generate a Pareto frontier of circuits with a deterministic compiler.
Analytically bound rare overflows and verify elementary gate sequences on representative circuits.
evidence_signal: Against Gidney’s 2025 baseline with matched adder accounting, the abstract reports a 70.1% reduction in minimum qubit–Toffoli product and up to 78.6% fewer expected factoring Toffolis at matched accumulator precision.
watch_item: These are logical circuit resource estimates; physical hardware costs and runtime remain dependent on fault-tolerant implementation choices.
paper_title: Reducing RSA-2048 Factoring Resources Below One Billion Toffolis via LLM-Driven Verifiable Quantum Compilation
